html:
A protest by Black schoolchildren in Soweto, near Johannesburg, that began on 16 June 1976 and grew into a revolt across South Africa.

Under apartheid, Black pupils were taught in a separate and poorer system. A rule of 1974 forced schools to teach half of their subjects in Afrikaans, which many saw as the language of the oppressor and which few teachers or pupils spoke well. Thousands of students marched in protest. Police fired on them. One of the first killed was the 12-year-old Hector Pieterson; the photograph of his body being carried became one of the defining images of apartheid.

Unrest spread to other cities for months. Hundreds of people were killed, most of them young. Thousands of students fled abroad and joined the armed wing of the African National Congress. The uprising was inspired by the Black Consciousness Movement, whose leader Steve Biko died in police custody the next year. 16 June is now Youth Day in South Africa.
sum: A protest by Black schoolchildren in Soweto, near Johannesburg, that began on 16 June 1976 and grew into a revolt across South Africa.
